body:
The interactive leaves (`planner`, `signoff`, `publisher`, `act` — every leaf with `interactive = true`) hand the terminal to a model+human REPL, and the driver's entire completion signal is process exit:

```python
if leaf.interactive:
    subprocess.run(argv + [prompt], cwd=workdir, env=run_env)
    return
```

`src/pdca_harness/leaves.py:199` — no `check=`, no capture. The exit code is discarded, so "the human pressed Ctrl-D" and "the leaf discharged its contract" are the same event as far as the driver is concerned. Whether the work actually happened is discovered later, by artifact reads further from the cause: the flow validates `signoff-decision` against `VALID_DECISIONS` (`leaves.py:65,71`) only once the session is gone, and a planner session that ends with a malformed or absent `brief.md` advances the bundle regardless.

Every interactive leaf has a checkable contract, and none of them is checked at the boundary:

| leaf | must have produced on exit |
|---|---|
| `planner` | `brief.md`, structurally against `templates/brief.md.tpl` |
| `signoff` | `signoff-decision` — one token from `VALID_DECISIONS`; rationale lines below the token for `iterate-*`/`discontinue`; §6 boxes ticked only on explicit human OK; §9 untouched (the driver records it under the C6 guard) |
| `publisher` | `commit-msg.txt` + `pr-description.md` |
| `act` | a dated entry appended to `process/act-log.md` |

## Proposal

1. **`template/.claude/commands/handoff.md.jinja`** — a `/handoff [<issue_id>]` command the leaf runs as its last act: verify this leaf's contract, report PASS/FAIL explicitly, write the completion marker, then end. Which contract applies is derivable from the render (the leaves configured `interactive = true` and their `agent` names), so it is rendered per instance rather than hardcoding the four above.

2. **A `Stop` hook to make it non-optional** — `template/.claude/hooks/handoff_guard.py`. A slash command is a prompt expansion: it cannot terminate its own session, and it cannot be relied on to be typed. A `Stop` hook fires when the model finishes and can block with feedback, so a session cannot quietly end with a missing or malformed marker. Same mechanical-discipline pattern as the existing `PreToolUse` `builder_guard.py`, moved to the exit boundary. Needs an escape hatch for deliberately abandoning a session.

3. **Capture the session's carry-forward.** `driver._carry_forward_into_brief` (`driver.py:174`, called on both iterate transitions at `:76`/`:81`) already folds the §9 sign-off rationale and the failing gates into the brief's `## Iteration N — carry-forward` block — but only from *recorded artifacts*, at the transition, after the session is gone. What the interactive session established and never wrote down — what was considered and rejected, which open questions remain, why the brief reads the way it does — is lost. `/handoff` runs while that context is still live, which makes it the right place to capture it; the driver then merges the session's contribution with what it already extracts.

**Batch wrinkle:** `do_plan_batch` and `run_signoff_batch` put N bundles through one interactive session, so the command takes an optional bundle id — `/handoff issue_508` gates one bundle, the bare form gates every bundle the session covered.

## On resuming sessions instead

Considered and rejected for the automated leaves; recording the rationale here because it will come up again.

- **Incompatible with the escalation ladder.** `[[leaves.builder_escalation]] min_iteration = 2` moves sonnet/high → opus/max. A resumed session cannot change model, and a fresh stronger attempt is the entire point of the ladder.
- **It re-anchors the retry on the reasoning that failed.** An iterate exists *because* the prior pass was wrong. Decorrelation is load-bearing here — a cross-vendor reviewer so it does not grade its own homework, an adversary defaulting to refuted — and resume imports the failed pass's commitments and confidence into the retry.
- **State would leave the bundle.** Session history is host-local, keyed to a project path that per-cycle worktree isolation tears down, invisible to `pdca act index`, and it breaks `--rehearse` and lane reproducibility.

Carry-forward-as-artifact (item 3) is the same continuity benefit inside the existing design, and it is already half-built.

Prototype: getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#166 — instance-local `.claude/commands/handoff.md`, no engine change, to settle the shape before it renders into every instance.

comments.body:
Prototype findings from the instance, for the shape this should take when it renders.

The prototype (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#166) merged after four review rounds and 27 findings. Several changed the design rather than just fixing it, so they are worth carrying into the upstream version rather than rediscovering:

**Scan mode was removed; ids are required.** A bare scan cannot know which bundles a session touched, and it was wrong in both directions — a newly authored brief was exempted from the checks that only apply to the session's own work, while an unrelated pre-existing valid artifact supplied a PASS even when the session wrote nothing. Deriving the touched set needs a baseline taken at session **start**, which an end-of-session command cannot take. That is driver knowledge, and it is the strongest argument for item 3 below.

**No artifact is written into the bundle.** An earlier version recorded a `handoff.json` marker; that is an artifact no role names, and a fourth write for sign-off, whose contract is "exactly three things, nothing else". Invoking a deterministic helper from inside a leaf does not make its output a driver artifact. The gate's verdict is its exit status and its report.

**The carry-forward half was dropped from the prototype for the same reason** — registering `handoff-notes.md` would have meant widening a deliberately tight write boundary for a file with no consumer. It belongs in item 3 of this issue, where the *consuming* half is built: registering and consuming are one change.

**The Act check needs a session-start baseline too.** Date membership is not authorship (Act runs more than once a day), and HEAD is not the session boundary (the leaf appends without committing, so a prior uncommitted entry already makes the tree longer). The prototype has the leaf NAME the entry it wrote, which removes the automatic pass but cannot catch a leaf naming an earlier session's uncommitted entry. Same driver-side baseline as above.

**Contract fields need checking against the corpus, not reasoned about.** Four required-field candidates would each have failed committed bundles: `Test file` (7 ship it empty on purpose), `Falsifiability` (52 of 85 predate the field), `**User impact:**` (43 predate the rule), and any multi-line value, which the line-based `brief.parse_fields` reads as empty. A rendered gate needs the named/scanned distinction — or a template-version check — so a bundle is never judged against a contract that postdates it.

**Reuse the instance's own lint rather than running the T4 gate.** `cli._contribcheck` already encodes the deterministic half of the publisher contract; the configured `T4-batch-review` is a multi-pass model review over `patch.diff` and never reads the prose.

Open follow-ups on the prototype: getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#172 (four defects still in the instance, including the `argument-hint` still advertising the removed scan mode).

Related: #340 extends the **planner** row of the exit-contract table above.

This issue defines the planner's contract as "`brief.md`, structurally against `templates/brief.md.tpl`". #340 adds a semantic clause to the same contract: every backticked token in `External dependencies` must resolve to a registered `[[doctor.checks]]` row whose detect `cmd` exits 0, or be annotated exempt.

Why it wants to live here rather than only as a driver-side hold: the check has to run while the human is **still at the terminal**, so an unmet dependency is installed or annotated on the spot instead of the human returning later to a held bundle. That is the ergonomic half; #340 keeps a deterministic Plan-exit hold as the authoritative half, since a model-run session contract must not be the only thing between a fabricated red→green proof and a green bundle.

No change to this issue's scope — noting it so the `/handoff` contract is not designed as structure-only.

title: Leaf exit contract: a `/handoff` gate for the interactive leaves, and capture the interactive session's carry-forward
